On the defence side, \cite{Kumar2026_siml} detects rogue nodes and limits acknowledgements at the gateway. The thesis of Chen \cite{ChenThesis2024} (we read its Chapter VII) describes the same attack family: confirmed uplinks sent at a high rate to use up the gateway's downlink duty, a MAC-command variant that forces the acknowledgements to SF12, and a variant with a malicious application server; it counters them with a threshold and outlier detector and a graded denylist that finally blocks the acknowledgement to the detected nodes. These attacks aim at the gateway's downlink; the attack here aims at the node's uplink budget through suppressed acknowledgements, and the reserve is a node-side defence. These attacks and defences are known, and we claim none of them. This paper contributes the node-side reserved budget for the follow-up frame of a two-stage alert, a bounded model check with a control, and preregistered results under India's rules.
